summary: Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a scholar in Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Presidency College, Chennai, and University of Calcutta, and under Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Pelden Chophel. He held posts at Bhutia Boarding School and the Government of Bengal.
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Manipur University, studying under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).
Saroja Bhate (born 1942) works in Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from around 1992 to 2002 and was attested there as professor in 2011.
Sarva Daman Singh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at Mill Hill School, Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, University of Madras, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University from circa 1971 to 1983.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied at Voorhees College, Madras Christian College, and University of Madras. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and was Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities.

Saswati Mutsuddy works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Dipak Kumar Barua and was a member of the teaching staff in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).
Satiranjan Sen was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied at Peking University. He was a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.
Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948). He served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953 to 1961.

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Presidency University.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1944–1955) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

Satoru Harada (born 1947) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning an M.A. from the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and studied under Esho Mikogami (attested 1996). Noriyama held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, working under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, and Luis O. Gómez, and became professor (1996) and president (2014) at Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Satoshi Ito (born 1961) works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1990 and served as a professor at Ibaraki University (attested 2007).
Satoshi Kawano specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Naiki earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he served as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).
Satya Narayan Goenka (1924–2013) was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under U Ba Khin from circa 1955 to 1971 and founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

Satya Swarup Misra (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.
